transcript.text:
Hi everyone. The AI-assisted code review feature has passed its planned functional tests and is ready for a limited production rollout. I have final approval authority for the rollout policy, and as part of our normal launch process, I need to conduct a final round-robin check with security, customer support, and data science before I can approve.

The draft rollout policy proposes enabling the feature for a random 10% customer cohort, storing review telemetry in us-east-1 for 90 days, and expanding access if adoption exceeds 20%.

I'd like to go through each team in turn. Could security, customer support, and data science each review this draft policy and flag any required revisions? Once we've covered all required revisions and they're recorded in the rollout ticket, I can settle the approval.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a required revision to the rollout policy. I confirmed with account teams an hour ago that exactly two contracted customers — Atlas Health and Cedar Bank — require explicit opt-in and a direct notice before this feature can be enabled for their users. I found this in the account playbooks while handling unrelated renewal questions and haven't yet updated the rollout ticket. The draft policy's random 10% cohort could inadvertently include users from these customers without the required opt-in and direct notice, so we need to revise the policy to exclude them from the default rollout or ensure their opt-in and notice process is completed before enabling.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a required security revision to the rollout policy. While reviewing telemetry samples for a different audit this morning, I confirmed that review snippets from regulated tenants are classified as confidential and must be encrypted, stored in eu-central-1, and deleted after exactly 7 days. The draft policy's telemetry_region field is a single value for the whole policy, not separate regional values by tenant, so that field must be set to eu-central-1. The settlement decisions must reflect eu-central-1 as the telemetry region, exactly 7 days for retention, and encryption — rather than the draft values of us-east-1 and 90 days. I have not yet attached the classification note to the launch document, so I'll need to do that or assign it as a follow-up commitment.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a required data science revision to the rollout policy. My analysis of the pilot data — completed only minutes ago — found that auto-enrolled users make the draft's adoption metric (adoption exceeding 20%) unusable as a success gate. The valid gate is task success of at least 85% on a manually sampled set of exactly 40 review tasks. The adoption criterion must be replaced with this exact task-success gate. Per company launch policy, rollout approval must remain withheld — rollout_approved must be false — until this gate revision is fully implemented and recorded in the rollout ticket, not merely assigned as a follow-up commitment.
